newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks see modest losses by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks see modest losses by close.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower in choppy trade on Tuesday after having spent most of the day confined to an eight point trading range.
While softer metals prices ensured a shaky start to the day, the resource leaders quickly came off their lows.
Afternoon strength in the banking sector ensured the day's losses were modest.
The All Ordinaries index fell 5.0 points to 2,380.1.
"The market is very strong in some stocks," said dealer Peter Struk of brokerage Reynolds and Co, citing Commonwealth Bank and ANZ Bank as examples.
"They (the banks) kept it together in the afternoon," another dealer said. "National Australia Bank saw profit taking but the rest looked pretty good," he added.
A note of caution was sounded as to whether the softer trend in the resources sector was likely to be reversed, with the strong Australian dollar seen as an obstacle to recovery.
"Commodities are not going to do a great deal while the Australian dollar is so high," Struk said.
Gold stocks were the biggest losers on the day.
The gold index closed 1.9 percent weaker, compared to a loss in the benchmark All Ordinaries index of just 0.2 percent.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
